messages:
incident-bot: ALERT - node-group decode-usw2-rt reported repeated GPU OOMs (5m spike). severity: high. paging oncall Maya (oncall).

Maya (oncall): seeing the alert. I’m paged. checking logs now.

Priya (runtime): confirmed — several streaming decode pods for route `gpt-realtime-v1` hit cudaOutOfMemory in the decode loop. stack shows growth during streaming chunks (KV cache not trimming).

Jordan (SRE): link to live grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/streaming/decode-nodes?orgId=1
- p95 GPU mem usage jumped from 12GB -> 30GB on a subset of pods
- OOM count: 17 in last 7m

Maya (oncall): @Priya quick question — any recent config pushes to max_tokens or streaming config?

Priya (runtime): yes, earlier today we accidentally pushed a routing config that removed the global max_tokens cap for the `realtime` route (PR #4221). clients can now set token_limit per-request, and some client tests set it to 1e6.

Eve (Eng): oh no. that explains runaway generation on a few requests. the runtime doesn't enforce a hard upper bound if client supplies large token_limit.

Jordan (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) block incoming traffic to affected pods via k8s label selector 2) scale down replicas 3) redeploy runtime hotfix that enforces server-side token hardcap 4) route traffic to fallback model variant (gpt-realtime-small)

Sam (platform): I'll add a temporary route rule to send new requests to `gpt-realtime-small` in us-west2 and europe while we contain. Applying now.

deploy-bot: rolling update started for route-routing patch -> applying 50% traffic shift to fallback. rollout id: r-2025-07-22-1823

Jordan (SRE): executing containment commands:
```
# cordon nodes with high OOMs
kubectl get pods -l app=decode,gpu=true -n redwood | grep OOM | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r kubectl delete pod -n redwood
# quick firewall to stop new traffic to label=decode-realtime
kubectl annotate svc realtime-rewrite redwood.io/maintenance=true -n redwood
```

Maya (oncall): deleted 6 pods, GPU mem pressure dropped on remaining ones. OOMs still reported from older pods coming back up, so we need the hotfix applied.

Priya (runtime): hotfix PR merging in 2m: server hardcap set to 2048 tokens for any request if client token_limit > 2048. patch:
```
if request.token_limit > SERVER_MAXTOKENS:
    request.token_limit = SERVER_MAXTOKENS
```
also added guard on KV cache growth: evict oldest prefixes when mem > 11GB.

deploy-bot: hotfix merged and deployed to decode-usw2 pool. version: runtime-3.14.1-hotfix

Jordan (SRE): observing pod restarts drop to 0 after deploy. GPU OOM rate down to 0 in last 3m.

Customer Ops: any confirmed customer impact? we saw increased 5xx for a small set of tenants around 18:23-18:36 PST. preparing comms.

Maya (oncall): quick impact summary: approx 1.4k requests dropped or returned 5xx in us-west2 between 18:21-18:35. Affected route: /v1/realtime/generate with model `gpt-realtime-v1`. Root cause: misconfig removed server-side token cap and allowed unbounded client token requests leading to unbounded KV growth and GPU OOMs.

Priya (runtime): logs sample from one failed pod: 
```
[ERROR] decode_loop.cpp:142 gpu_memory_alloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
stack: decode::stream_chunk -> kv_cache::ensure_capacity -> attention_kv::grow
```
Also a request sample that caused runaway (redacted client id): `{"token_limit": 1000000, "prompt": "..."}`

Eve (Eng): note — one dev test client had an automated fuzzing script hitting API w/ huge token_limit. we should add rate-limits per-tenant to avoid single-tenant storms.

Sam (platform): temporary rate-limit added for realtime route: 30 reqs/min per tenant + enforced token hardcap.

Jordan (SRE): followups for P1 -> start RCA and postmortem:
- revert accidental PR that removed server cap (PR #4221) -> done
- formalize server-side hardcap and KV eviction (deployed) -> done
- add unit/integration tests that simulate streaming with huge token_limit -> assigned to Eve
- add alert rule: GPU_mem_growth_rate > X for 5m -> page oncall -> assigned to Jordan
- conversation with API product about removing ability for clients to set token_limit beyond tenant quota -> assigned to Priya + Product

Customer Ops: drafting customer-facing note: "We identified a misconfiguration that allowed unbounded token requests which caused some requests to fail between 18:21-18:35 PST. We mitigated the issue by enforcing a server-side token limit and routing traffic to a smaller model variant. We're continuing a full RCA." will send after final numbers.

Maya (oncall): handing off to Jordan for night coverage. I’ll update postmortem checklist and attach incident logs.

Jordan (SRE): taking over. quick status: system stable, routing still on fallback for 10% traffic while we validate. monitoring for 1 hour, then shift back gradually.

Priya (runtime): quick note for postmortem: add invariant tests in runtime that assert: max_tokens <= SERVER_MAX_DEFAULT and KV cache evicts when mem > threshold. Also propose an emergency kill-switch that returns 422 for token_limit > hardcap instead of allowing runtime to try generation.

Eve (Eng): I'll own the test work. ETA: 3 working days for tests + small framework changes.

Jordan (SRE): final operational numbers to include in postmortem:
- total failed requests: ~1,420
- unique tenants impacted: 6 (sandbox + 5 customers)
- downtime (elevated errors): 14min (18:21-18:35 PST)
- mitigation elapsed time (alert -> hotfix deployed): 14 min

Customer Ops: message sent to impacted customers.

Maya (oncall): closing my watch. handoff complete. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Jordan (SRE): marking incident as mitigated. next steps: full RCA doc, link to PRs, test checklist, follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:30am PT.

Priya (runtime): adding postmortem draft to docs repo and will include logs and the failing request examples (redacted).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) - severity downgraded to sev2.

Maya (oncall): filing ticket to prevent customers from setting token_limit > tenant_quota at API gateway level (assigned to Sam).

Customer Ops: thanks all — customers appreciate the quick fix.
